slides.title: From measurements to questions worth asking.
slides.body: Open a dedicated target log, or go straight to a field scan. The numbered sections guide you through the process.
slides.note: Actual hosted analyzer. All observations shown in this walkthrough are fictional, generated for demonstration.

slides.title: See the target’s night unfold.
slides.body: A named-target CSV produces a light curve with measurements and clock-aligned median bins. Here a deliberately simulated dip fades and recovers.
slides.note: Smaller magnitude means brighter. The dip was built into the demo data; this is not a real eclipse detection.

slides.title: Check what the frame files add.
slides.body: This run reads 180 synthetic frame CSVs and associates 4,320 measurements into 24 provisional tracks. All 180 target-log rows match their frame counterparts.
slides.note: Captured using “Select frame CSVs instead.” The native folder picker and FITS/JPEG inventory were not demonstrated. Matching exports are the same observation, not independent confirmation.

slides.title: Let your eye explore the curves.
slides.body: Actual miniature curves share a timeline and magnitude-change scale. Tile size, scaling and review-priority sorting help you choose what to inspect.
slides.note: Review priority is an exploratory heuristic, not an eclipse probability. These fictional stars include dips, waves, trends and nearly flat curves.

slides.title: One click opens the detail.
slides.body: Select a thumbnail to open its full light curve. The gallery can close automatically, leaving the main chart ready for inspection.
slides.note: Coordinate-based tracks remain provisional. A good-looking curve does not validate its identity or establish an astrophysical cause.

slides.title: Return without losing your star.
slides.body: Back to gallery reopens the miniature curves and returns to the current selection. Its outline and Selected label make it easy to find again.
slides.note: This screenshot shows the actual selected-tile state after the browser’s return scroll completed.

slides.title: Keep a useful record.
slides.body: The analyzer offers chart PNG, processed-bin CSV and report exports for closer investigation or sharing. Optional catalogue lookups are available elsewhere in the app.
slides.note: This slide shows enabled export controls; export downloads and catalogue lookups were not exercised in this walkthrough. It is an exploration/preparation tool, not calibrated discovery confirmation.
